content.value_statement: Project context becomes stale, duplicated, or disconnected across sessions. This skill organizes authorized notes, preserves provenance, and routes canonical changes through their owning registries.
actual_capabilities: Initializes private runtime memory from project templates after authorization.
Retrieves current priorities by following HOT pointers to dated evidence or registry records.
Captures, promotes, demotes, and archives notes under explicit permission and age rules.
Consolidates comparable notes while preserving conflicts, source references, and registry ownership.
Audits broken links, orphaned artifacts, stale summaries, and mismatched registry revisions.
Runs privacy-aware erasure workflows with dry searches, suppression checks, minimal logs, and precise scope reporting.
limitations: Does not change canonical registry facts or accept proposals for registry owners.
Requires compatible repository scripts and shared references for registry initialization and validation.
Cannot guarantee deletion from Git history, backups, or systems outside the authorized working tree.
Does not provide legal advice or replace organizational retention and privacy procedures.

use_cases.title: Resume active project work
use_cases.description: Review HOT priorities and follow evidence pointers before continuing a project in a new session.

use_cases.title: Consolidate research notes
use_cases.description: Deduplicate comparable notes, preserve conflicts, repair links, and archive stale artifacts without changing canonical facts.

use_cases.title: Handle authorized erasure
use_cases.description: Dry-run a subject search, verify suppression, erase authorized copies, and document scope limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Review current memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Review authorized project memory. Show current HOT priorities, source dates, and evidence pointers. Do not write or modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Capture an approved conclusion
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this approved conclusion: [conclusion]. Cite [source], record the date, choose HOT or WARM, and report the authorized path.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate a memory scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Consolidate authorized notes under [scope]. Preserve conflicts, identify broken links, propose registry-owned changes, and report every changed path.

prompt_templates.title: Execute an authorized purge
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare and execute an authorized purge for [pseudonymous ID]. Dry-run first, verify suppression, minimize logs, rebuild projections, and report limitations.

output_examples.input: Review saved project context without changing files.
output: Evidence: dated WARM brief with an accepted registry pointer.
Status: read-only review completed; no files changed.

output_examples.input: Archive authorized WARM notes older than 90 days.
output_examples.output: Archived three eligible notes after retention checks. Original paths, hashes, and source pointers were preserved. Registry streams and projections were unchanged.
The dry search found four authorized working copies. Suppression was verified before deletion. The report distinguishes working-tree erasure from history and backups.

best_practices: Begin with read-only review and verify live registry offsets before relying on cached summaries.
Obtain explicit authorization before persistent writes, archival, or erasure.
Keep HOT concise and link each conclusion to dated WARM evidence or accepted registry records.
anti_patterns: Do not treat cached absence as negative evidence or current truth.
Do not edit registry event streams, projections, or user-approved decisions directly.
Do not store credentials, raw contact data, or production exports in runtime memory.

faq.question: What information can this skill store?
faq.answer: It stores authorized project-local notes, evidence pointers, decisions, indexes, and privacy operation records.

faq.question: Can it change canonical registry facts?
faq.answer: No. It submits proposals to owning registries and preserves their event ownership boundaries.

faq.question: Does it write files automatically?
faq.answer: Only when the current request explicitly authorizes the named operation. Read-only reviews and dry runs need no write permission.

faq.question: How does it protect personal data?
faq.answer: It minimizes stored data, verifies consent suppression, avoids raw identifiers in logs, and requires explicit erasure authority.

faq.question: Does purge remove Git history and backups?
faq.answer: No. It removes authorized working copies and reports that history or backups may require separate controller procedures.

faq.question: Can a standalone skill folder initialize registries?
faq.answer: No. Registry initialization requires the compatible host repository, shared references, verified scripts, and event schemas.
